articles.title: Precious metals rate today: Gold holds near 10-week high; silver rises
articles.full_text: Gold climbed to its highest level since June 5 in the previous session before giving up some gains. Spot prices touched $4,435 an ounce before retreating as crude oil prices advanced amid uncertainty over the Strait of Hormuz. Gold had risen for six consecutive sessions in the Indian market, reflecting stronger safe-haven and investment demand. Rising oil prices are adding another layer of uncertainty for bullion markets as concerns over the US-Iran conflict and shipping disruptions persist. Higher energy prices can fuel inflation and encourage central banks to keep interest rates elevated for longer. That could weigh on gold, which does not offer interest income. Investors are therefore closely watching developments around the Strait of Hormuz alongside US economic data. The US Consumer Price Index data due later on Wednesday is expected to be the key event for gold markets, as traders look for clues about the Federal Reserve’s next interest-rate move. Markets have reduced bets on a September Fed rate hike to 48% after weaker-than-expected US jobs data. A softer inflation reading could reinforce expectations for easier monetary policy, potentially supporting gold. Gold prices edged higher on Wednesday as investors awaited US inflation data for fresh clues on the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate outlook. Spot gold gained 0.3% to $4,377.79 per ounce by 0055 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery were little changed at $4,438. Bullion had climbed to its highest level since June 5 on Tuesday before encountering technical resistance around the 100-day moving average near $4,387.

articles.title: Vande Mataram gets legal protection on par with national anthem: Here is what students must know
articles.description: President Droupadi Murmu has approved the 2026 amendment extending statutory protection under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act to Vande Mataram. The story explains the amended provisions, the Home Ministry’s protocols, the song’s historical significance and what students should know about the new rules.
